prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the near-field geometry of the excavator cab interior, showing the camera wearer's torso and thighs at 0.2 to 0.5 metres below, the control levers, foot pedals, and display monitor within arm's reach at 0.4 to 0.8 metres in front and below, and the cab pillars and central boom extending from 0.5 to 2.0 metres. As the cab rotates left across the five frames, the left cab frame shifts into the immediate foreground on the left while the boom remains centrally positioned in front of the wearer. In frame 3, the map faintly resolves the silhouette of the standing person in the blue shirt at roughly 3 to 4 metres in front and slightly left of the boom, facing left away from the wearer, before the left pillar and frame boundary occlude them in frames 4 and 5. Compared to the RGB image, the depth map more clearly separates the 3D layering of the wearer's arms, knees, and cab controls from the background lawn without visual clutter from grass textures and shadows. However, the map is unreliable on the right cab window glass in frames 1 and 2—treating the transparent pane and glare as a near, solid surface—and it fails to resolve the crouching person at 4 to 5 metres or the depth contours of the excavated hole and bucket in the dark background.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates parts of the camera wearer's lower body and arms in the lower foreground at 0.2 to 0.6 metres, along with the standing person in the upper-left background of frame 3 at roughly 3 to 4 metres in front of the cab. In frame 3, this standing person is positioned just left of the excavator boom, facing left toward the excavated dirt and away from the camera wearer, while the wearer's hands remain within arm's reach of the control joysticks and their own knees below. Across the five frames, as the cab turns counter-clockwise, the segmentation of the wearer's legs and arms fragments and shifts labels between frames, and in frame 5 it splits the wearer's left leg, right leg, and right hand on the lever into three separate 'person' instances. While the map highlights the standing worker's silhouette in frame 3 and the boundary of the small control monitor at 0.6 metres in frame 2, it provides much less spatial detail than the RGB view. It is highly unreliable overall: in frame 1 it misclassifies the entire excavator cab, boom, and right window as a 'motorcycle', in frame 2 it mislabels the cab's digital display screen as a 'cell phone', and across all frames it completely misses the crouching person 1.5 to 2 metres left of the standing worker as well as the standing worker's legs in frame 2.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map detects only a single magenta 2D hand skeleton across all five frames, corresponding to the camera wearer's right hand positioned roughly 0.4 to 0.5 metres in front of and below the viewpoint. This hand remains within immediate reach of the cab's right-center control lever and display monitor, grasping the joystick from above with fingers curled downward and forward. Across the five frames, as the excavator cab rotates to the left, the tracked right hand shifts slightly from the lower-left-center of the frame toward the lower-right while maintaining a steady grip orientation relative to the control console. The pose map isolates the exact finger articulation and wrist orientation of the operating hand on the dark joystick more clearly than the shadowed RGB control area. However, it is severely incomplete, failing to detect the wearer's partially occluded left hand resting on their left thigh at 0.4 metres, the wearer's own lower-body skeleton, and both external workers at 3 to 5 metres (so it provides no pose information on their facing directions, gaze, or reach).
